title: The Pythagorean theorem
lede: In every right triangle, a² + b² = c². It lets you find any distance you can't measure directly.

sections.md:
## The rule
In a **right triangle**, the side across from the right angle is the **hypotenuse** (c). It's always the longest side. The other two are the **legs** (a and b).

**a² + b² = c²**

It only works for right triangles.

## Why it's true
Build a big square with side a + b. Put four copies of the triangle inside, one in each corner. The space left in the middle is a tilted square of side c, area c². Rearrange the same four triangles and the leftover space becomes two squares, a² and b². Same big square, same four triangles, so the leftover areas match: **a² + b² = c²**.

## Triples worth memorizing
Whole-number right triangles: **3-4-5**, **5-12-13**, **8-15-17**, **7-24-25**. Multiples work too: 6-8-10, 9-12-15. Spotting one saves a calculation.

sections.title: Find a leg
sections.problem: A 13 ft ladder leans on a wall. Its foot is 5 ft from the wall. How high does it reach?
steps: The ladder is the hypotenuse: 5² + h² = 13².

sections.label: Is it a right triangle?
sections.md: Check whether the two shorter sides squared add up to the longest side squared. 9, 12, 15: 81 + 144 = 225 = 15². Yes. This is how builders square a corner: measure 3 ft one way, 4 ft the other, and the diagonal must be 5 ft.
